prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
competitors_mentioned: Require a Manual J Load Calculation
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your exact location in Atlanta, your home size and ductwork, your budget, brand preference, and whether you want highest efficiency or lowest upfront cost.

I can help find a great contractor for you, but first a few quick questions:
- What Atlanta ZIP code or neighborhood are you in?
- Is this a full system replacement (outdoor condenser + indoor coil/furnace) or just the outdoor unit?
- Do you have a brand you prefer (Trane, Carrier, Lennox, Goodman, etc.) or a SEER target?
- Any timeline or budget constraints?

While you decide, here are practical tips to pick the best company and get a good installation:
- Get at least 3 on-site written estimates. Avoid quotes based only on phone descriptions.
- Require a Manual J load calculation (proper sizing) and ask for the Manual D duct plan if ducts are being changed.
- Verify licensing and insurance for Georgia/Atlanta and ask for proof. Check city permits: good contractors pull permits.
- Ask for NATE-certified technicians, and for membership in ACCA or other trade organizations (good sign).
- Compare equipment by model number and SEER rating, not just price. Ask for AHRI ratings if needed.
- Check warranties: equipment warranty vs. workmanship warranty (look for at least 1–2 years on labor).
- Read recent Google/BBB/Angi reviews and ask for local references.
- Confirm they will test airflow, refrigerant charge, and provide start-up paperwork and manuals.
- Ask about rebates, tax credits, and financing options.

If you give your ZIP code and the points above, I’ll compile a short list (3–5) of highly rated Atlanta HVAC companies, summarizing their strengths and recent ratings so you can pick the best fit. Which ZIP code are you in?
